“A budget is telling your money where to go instead of wondering where it went.” — Dave Ramsey
“Small daily leaks sink great financial ships. Track even the minor costs.” — BudgetBasics Rule

moneyMistakes.title: Impulse Buying & Sale Traps
moneyMistakes.scenario: Buying a $60 jacket simply because it was advertised as '50% off', even though you did not need a jacket and had not budgeted for it.
moneyMistakes.impact: Leaves you short on essential textbook purchases or rent at month-end.
moneyMistakes.fix: Institute the **48-Hour Rule**: wait two full days before completing any non-essential purchase over $30. In 80% of cases, the impulse fades.

moneyMistakes.title: Ignoring Small Daily Cash Leaks
moneyMistakes.scenario: Buying a $5.50 specialty iced caramel latte every weekday morning before campus lecture.
moneyMistakes.impact: $5.50 × 20 class days = **$110 per month** or **$1,320 per academic year** spent entirely on coffee.
moneyMistakes.fix: Brew quality coffee at home in an insulated tumbler. Treat cafe drinks as a once-a-week reward to save $85+ each month.

moneyMistakes.title: Zombie / Unused Subscriptions
moneyMistakes.scenario: Signing up for 3 video streaming services, a cloud storage tier, and a gym pass that hasn't been visited in 4 months.
moneyMistakes.impact: Silent recurring monthly auto-charges siphon $45-$90 without active awareness.
moneyMistakes.fix: Conduct a **Monthly Subscription Audit**. Cancel recurring apps you haven't opened in the past 14 days.

moneyMistakes.title: Spending Without a Written Monthly Plan
moneyMistakes.scenario: Assuming you will 'just be frugal' without allocating specific spending limits to food, transit, and social activities.
moneyMistakes.impact: Money disappears into unexplained transactions, leading to end-of-month panic.
moneyMistakes.fix: Adopt the **50-30-20 Guideline**: 50% for Needs, 30% for Wants, and 20% for Savings immediately upon receiving income.

moneyMistakes.title: Neglecting an Emergency Buffer Fund
moneyMistakes.scenario: Living paycheck-to-paycheck with $0 saved for unexpected medical bills, laptop repairs, or transit breakdowns.
moneyMistakes.impact: Forces students into high-interest payday loans or credit card debt balances.
moneyMistakes.fix: Build a beginner **$500 Starter Emergency Fund** first before expanding non-essential recreational spending.
